Court No. - 81
Case :- Criminal Appeal No. - 5187 of 2024

Appellant :- Tanveer Ahmad
Respondent :- State of U.P. and Another
Counsel for Appellant :- Muktesh Kumar Singh

Counsel for Respondent :- G.A.,Kamlesh Shrama
Hon'ble Manoj Bajaj,J.
Tanveer Ahmad- Appellant has filed this appeal under Section 14-A(2) Scheduled Castes and
Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 to challenge the order dated 23.04.2024
passed by Special Judge, (Sc/St Act), Jaunpur, whereby his application under Section 439 Cr.P.C.
for regular bail, during pendency of trial in case crime no.80 of 2024, under Sections 366, 376-D
I.P.C. and Section 3(2)(V) S.C./S.T. Act, Police Station Sarai Khwaja, District Jaunpur has been
dismissed.

Learned counsel for the accused- appellant has argued that the complainant, who is husband of prosecutrix has falsely implicated the appellant- accused, as the allegations contained in the F.I.R.
regarding missing of his wife and expression of suspicion upon a gang engaged in human trafficking have been disbelieved, and no such offence relating to human trafficking is incorporated in the first information report.

Learned counsel further submits that the wife of the complainant was recovered,
who gave her version of the alleged occurrence through her statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C. and clearly stated that she was enticed away by co- accused Guddu Yadav, but in the statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C., she has implicated the appellant with the same allegations and further introduced the allegation of rape.

He submits that the version by the prosecution witnesses are at material variance with each other, and it is not believable that the victim went missing on 28th Tanveer Ahmad vs State Of U.P. And Another on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87776419/
1 January, 2024 and could not raise any alarm, who was recovered on 10.3.2024.

sentences.text: Learned counsel while assailing the impugned order dated 23.4.2024 rejecting the application by accused under Section 439 Cr.P.C. has argued that the Special Court, Jaunpur has failed to notice the serious lapses in the prosecution case, and prays that the impugned order dated 23.4.2024 be set aside, and the appellant be released on bail.

Mr. Kamlesh Shrama, learned counsel for the complainant opposes the prayer and submits that the complainant has specifically named the accused- appellant in the F.I.R. and his version is further supported by the victim as well, who in her statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C. has also named the accused- appellant.

Similar is the stand of the learned State Counsel, who submits that the offence is serious and the victim has also assigned specific role to the accused- appellant, therefore, the Special Court, Jaunpur has rightly refused to extend the concession of regular bail to the accused.

According to the learned State Counsel, the appellant is the only accused so far arrested in the case, therefore,
the trial is yet to commence.
Lastly, it is prayed, that the appeal be dismissed.

Upon hearing the learned counsel for the parties and considering their submissions, this Court finds that the version given by the victim in her two statements may be at variance, but the truthfulness would emerge only after the prosecution discharges the onus.

The appellant- accused is in custody since 10.4.2024 and the trial is likely to consume considerable time to conclude, therefore, his further detention behind the bars would not serve any useful purpose.

The case set up by the prosecution mainly relies upon the evidence of the complainant and his wife besides the other official witnesses and during the course of hearing, nothing has been shown that there is any likelihood of their being won over.

A perusal of the impugned order dated 23.4.2024 would reveal that the Special Court, Jaunpur has simply placed reliance upon the statement of victim recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C., whereas the other material collected during investigation has not been carefully examined for the purpose of exercising the discretion.
Thus, this Court has no hesitation in holding that the impugned order dated 23.4.2024 being not based upon the correct appreciation of material on record is unsustainable.

Resultantly, without meaning any expression of opinion on the merits of the case, the impugned order dated 23.04.2024 is set aside, the bail application filed by the appellant- accused under Section 439 Code of Criminal Procedure is hereby accepted, and it is ordered that the appellant- Tanveer Ahmad be released on regular bail in the above case crime subject to his furnishing the requisite bail bonds and surety bonds to the satisfaction of the trial court.
The appeal is allowed.

Order Date :- 12.9.2024/Raj  Tanveer Ahmad vs State Of U.P. And Another on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87776419/
